next_information_needs: By prediction time, what cohort retention, engagement, organic acquisition and payer-conversion evidence had been disclosed that distinguishes deliberate removal of low-quality users from persistent underlying demand deterioration?

What product or monetization milestones, launch schedules and measurable adoption tests had been disclosed by prediction time that could change expectations within the forecast horizon, beyond general strategic intentions?

By prediction time, what savings estimates, implementation timetable, cash restructuring charges and realized progress had been disclosed, and what evidence showed that reduced staffing could preserve product delivery and member safety?

What available disclosures explain the payer and monetization trends through pricing, mix, churn and geographic or app-level differences, including whether monetization improvement came at the expense of retention?

supporting_evidence.claim: Management disclosed a shift away from paid member acquisition and performance marketing toward brand and organic investment, while warning of short-term pressure on revenue and paying users.
supporting_evidence.exact_text: To align with these priorities, we have strategically shifted away from paid member acquisition and performance marketing in favor of brand and organic investment. As we address these areas of focus, our member growth and success in attracting new members, member engagement and monetization may be negatively impacted. In addition, efforts to improve the health of our membership base, including the removal of bad actors from our apps and strategically reducing paid performance marketing for member acquisition, may adversely affect revenue and paying users in the short term.

supporting_evidence.claim: As of June 30, 2025, cash and cash equivalents were $261.7 million; management believed available resources sufficient for its business plans during the next twelve months, based on conditions then.
supporting_evidence.exact_text: As of June 30, 2025, we had $261.7 million of cash and cash equivalents, an increase of $57.4 million from December 31, 2024. Our principal sources of liquidity are our cash and cash equivalents and cash generated from operations. Our primary uses of liquidity are operating expenses and capital expenditures, acquisition of businesses, funding of our debt obligations, partnership tax distributions, paying income taxes and obligations under our tax receivable agreement and effectuating share repurchases as discussed below. Based on current conditions, we believe that we have sufficient financial resources to fund our activities and execute our business plans during the next twelve months.
